source_text: Τὸ μυστήριον οὖν τοῦ προβάτου, ὃ τὸ πάσχα θύειν ἐντέταλται ὁ θεὸς τύπος ἦν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὗ τῷ αἵματι κατὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν πίστεως χρίονται τοὺς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν , τουτέστιν ἑαυτούς, οἱ πιστεύοντες εἰς αὐτόν· ὅτι γὰρ τὸ πλάσμα, ὃ ἔπλασεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν Ἀδάμ, οἶκος ἐγένετο τοῦ ἐμφυσήματος τοῦ παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ , καὶ πάντες νοεῖν δύνασθε. Καὶ ὅτι πρόσκαιρος ἦν καὶ αὕτη ἡ ἐντολὴ, οὕτως ἀποδείκνυμι. Οὐδαμοῦ θύεσθαι τὸ πρόβατον τοῦ πάσχα ὁ θεὸς συγχωρεῖ, εἰ μὴ ἐπὶ τόπῳ ᾧ ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ , εἰδὼς ὅτι ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι μετὰ τὸ παθεῖν τὸν Χριστόν, ὅτε καὶ ὁ τόπος τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ τοῖς ἐχθροῖς ὑμῶν παραδοθήσεται καὶ παύσονται ἅπασαι ἁπλῶς προσφοραὶ γινόμεναι. Καὶ τὸ κελευσθὲν πρόβατον ἐκεῖνο ὀπτὸν ὅλον γίνεσθαι τοῦ πάθους τοῦ σταυροῦ, δι᾿ οὗ πάσχειν ἔμελλεν ὁ Χριστός, σύμβολον ἦν. Τὸ γὰρ ὀπτώμενον πρόβατον σχηματιζόμενον ὁμοίως τῷ σχήματι τοῦ σταυροῦ ὀπτᾶι· εἶς γὰρ ὄρθιος ὀβελίσκος διαπερονᾶται ἀπὸ τῶν κατωτάτω μερῶν μέχρι τῆς κεφαλῆς, καὶ εἷς πάλιν κατὰ τὸ μετάφρενον, ᾧ προσαρτῶνται καὶ αἱ χεῖρες τοῦ προβάτου. Καὶ οἱ ἐν τῇ νηστείᾳ δὲ τράγοι δύο ὅμοιοι κελευσθέντες [Léu., XVI, 5 sq.] γίνεσθαι, ὧν ὁ εἷς ἀποπομπαῖος ἐγίνετο, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος εἰς προσφοράν, τῶν δύο παρουσιῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ καταγγελία ἦσαν· μιᾶς μέν, ἐν ᾗ ὡς ἀποπομπαῖον αὐτὸν παρεπέμψαντο οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ ὑμῶν καὶ οἱ ἱερεῖς, ἐπιβαλόντες αὐτῷ τὰς χεῖρας καὶ θανατώσαντες αὐτόν, καὶ τῆς δευτέρας δὲ αὐτοῦ παρουσίας, ὅτι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ τόπῳ τῶν Ἱεροσολύμων ἐπιγνώσεσθε αὐτόν, τὸν ἀτιμωθέντα ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν, καὶ προσφορὰ ἦν ὑπὲρ πάντων τῶν μετανοεῖν βουλομένων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ νηστευόντων ἣν καταλέγει Ἡσαίας νηστείαν, διασπῶντες στραγγαλιὰς βιαίων συναλλαγμάτων καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ὁμοίως τὰ κατηριθμημένα ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ , ἃ καὶ αὐτὸς ἀνιστόρησα, φυλάσσοντες, ἃ ποιοῦσιν οἱ τῷ Ἰησοῦ πιστεύοντες. Καὶ ὅτι καὶ ἡ τῶν δύο τράγων τῶν νηστείᾳ κελευσθέντων προσφέρεσθαι προσφορὰ οὐδαμοῦ ὁμοίως συγκεχώρηται γίνεσθαι εἰ μὴ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις, ἐπίστασθε.
pass_a_gloss: The mystery of the lamb, which God commanded to be sacrificed as the Passover, was a type of Christ, with whose blood, according to the word of faith in Him, the houses of those who believe in Him, that is, themselves, are anointed; for the creature which God formed, Adam, became a house of the breath from God, and you all can understand. And that this command was temporary, I thus demonstrate. Nowhere does God permit the lamb of the Passover to be sacrificed except in the place where His name is called upon, knowing that days will come after Christ has suffered, when also the place of Jerusalem will be handed over to your enemies and all simple offerings will cease. And the command that the lamb be roasted whole was a symbol of the passion of the cross, through which Christ was about to suffer. For the roasted lamb, formed similarly to the shape of the cross, is roasted; for one upright spit is pierced from the lower parts to the head, and another across the shoulders, to which the hands of the lamb are also fastened. And the two goats commanded to be made during the fast, one of which became a scapegoat and the other a sacrifice, were a proclamation of the two comings of Christ; one, in which the elders of your people and the priests sent Him away as a scapegoat, laying hands on Him and killing Him, and the other of His second coming, that in the same place of Jerusalem you will recognize Him, whom you dishonored, and He will be a sacrifice for all sinners who want to repent and fast, which fast Isaiah speaks of, breaking the bonds of violent agreements and the other things similarly enumerated by him, which also I have recounted, keeping them, which those who believe in Jesus do. And that the sacrifice of the two goats commanded to be offered during the fast is not permitted to be made anywhere else but in Jerusalem, you know.

pass_b_english: The mystery of the lamb which God commanded to be sacrificed as the Passover was a type of Christ. Through his blood, according to the word of faith in him, believers anoint their own houses, that is, themselves. For the creature God formed, Adam, became a house of the breath from God, and you can all understand this. I demonstrate that this command was temporary in this way: God permits the Passover lamb to be sacrificed nowhere except in the place where his name is invoked. He knew that days would come after Christ suffered when the place of Jerusalem would be handed over to your enemies and all simple offerings would cease. The command that the lamb be roasted whole was a symbol of the passion of the cross through which Christ was about to suffer. The roasted lamb, shaped like the cross, is roasted on one upright spit pierced from the lower parts to the head and another across the shoulders to which the lamb's hands are fastened. The two goats commanded for the fast, one becoming a scapegoat and the other a sacrifice, proclaimed the two comings of Christ (Leviticus 16:5). In the first coming, the elders of your people and the priests sent him away as a scapegoat, laying hands on him and killing him. In his second coming, you will recognize him in the very place of Jerusalem, the one you dishonored, and he will be a sacrifice for all sinners who wish to repent and keep the fast Isaiah describes, breaking the bonds of violent agreements and the other matters similarly enumerated by him. I have also recounted these things, keeping them, which those who believe in Jesus do. You also know that the sacrifice of the two goats commanded for the fast is not permitted anywhere but in Jerusalem.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological arguments regarding the Passover lamb, the shape of the spit, and the two goats. Pass B correctly identifies the Levitical context for the two goats (Leviticus 16:5) which is alluded to in the Greek text. The translation of 'μετὰ τὸ παθεῖν τὸν Χριστόν' as 'after Christ suffered' and the description of the spit 'one upright... and another across' matches the Greek 'εἷς ὄρθιος... καὶ εἷς πάλιν κατὰ τὸ μετάφρενον'.
